title: Open WebUI model meta.knowledge -- T1005 attached foreign file_id authorizes read/delete via model metadata
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54012 (GHSA-vjqm-6gcc-62cr,
CVSS 7.1 HIGH), affecting Open WebUI prior to 0.9.6.

Any user who can create, update, or import a workspace model can store
arbitrary `meta.knowledge` entries on that model without Open WebUI
checking whether they own or can read the referenced files. Two
DOWNSTREAM code paths then trust those entries as an authorization
source: the built-in `view_file` tool reads the referenced file's
extracted text when the model is used, and `has_access_to_file()`'s
MODEL branch authorizes the file-content and file-delete endpoints
based on the same metadata. A malicious model owner can therefore
attach another user's `file_id` to their own model's `meta.knowledge`
and both read and DELETE that private file -- a mechanistically
distinct sibling of `observed_open_webui_shared_chat_file_ownership_bypass_t1005`
(which reaches the same class of bug through chat sharing rather than
model metadata).

Detection logic flags a model create/update/import request whose
`meta.knowledge` array references a `file_id` NOT owned by the
requesting user -- the exact check both downstream authorization paths
needed and neither performed.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.9.6.
